newsitem.title: UK: Britain aims to reverse exodus from Montserrat.
newsitem.headline: Britain aims to reverse exodus from Montserrat.

text.p: Britain said on Tuesday that it hopes to reverse the exodus of people from Montserrat by carefully developing the half of the Caribbean island unaffected by the active Soufriere Hills volcano.
"It is my own view that people who have left might well return when they know what our commitment is to the north," International Development Secretary Clare Short told a news conference.

She was speaking after a meeting with Bertrand Osborne, chief minister of the British colony where hot rock, gas and ash poured into the abandoned capital Plymouth, at the south end of the island, for the first time on Monday.

The island's population has fallen from 11,000 to 5,200 since the volcano burst into life in 1995 after nearly four centuries of dormancy. Thousands of people have left for other Caribbean islands and for Britain.

But Osborne said scientists had advised that about 15-16 square miles (39-41 sq km) in the north were safe. This gave the opportunity for a planned development of the island with suitable housing and with a view to attracting industry.
"We are looking forward to a new Montserrat and we are pretty confident that we will have a new Montserrat that most Montserratians will come back to," he said.

Britain's Foreign Secretary Robin Cook, who met Osborne on Monday, said in a statement: "The Government will continue to place the highest priority on sustaining, and improving, the economic and social structure of Montserrat."

Britain has given 37 million pounds ($60 million) in assistance to Montserrat over the past year. The latest seven million pounds, announced last month, will help build emergency shelter for the homeless and a temporary hospital.
Scientists say the volcano could rumble on for another five years, and that the south of the 11-by-7-mile (18-by-11-km) island will be unusable until it quietens down again.

Short said evacuation of the eastern Caribbean island had "never ever been contemplated", though Britain was committed to consulting individual families about their future. It is still considering whether to offer poor islanders a resettlement aid package if they wish to leave. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
